nodes.description: Public dynamic array LoveBlock[] locks storing all created love blocks.
Private mapping lockToOwner mapping lock index to owner address.
Private mapping ownerToNumber mapping owner address to number of blocks owned.
SafeMath.add(uint256 a, uint256 b) internal pure returns c = a + b with assert overflow check.
External view returning ownerToNumber[msg.sender].
External view returning locks.length.
External function creating a new LoveBlock, writing lockToOwner and incrementing ownerToNumber.
External view collecting and returning all lock indices owned by msg.sender.
msg.sender used as owner identity and mapping key.
block.timestamp accessed through now when creating a LoveBlock.
locks.push(LoveBlock(_message, _encrypted, now)) appends state to storage array.
Storage write lockToOwner[id] = msg.sender.
Storage write ownerToNumber[msg.sender] = ownerToNumber[msg.sender].add(1).
String parameter _message of createLoveBlock.
Bool parameter _encrypted of createLoveBlock.
Local id holding the new lock index from locks.push - 1.
Local uint[] memory result array of owned lock indices in myLoveBlocks.
Local counter tracking the write position in result.
Local loop index i iterating over locks in myLoveBlocks.
First parameter a of SafeMath.add.
Second parameter b of SafeMath.add.
Local c = a + b of SafeMath.add that is asserted and returned.

edges.reason: createLoveBlock executes locks.push to store the new LoveBlock struct.
createLoveBlock writes the owner for the newly created lock id.
createLoveBlock increments the caller's block count.
msg.sender is stored as the owner in lockToOwner[id], granting ownership derived from caller identity.
msg.sender is used as the mapping key when incrementing ownerToNumber.
block.timestamp (now) is written into the LoveBlock storage entry, creating timestamp dependency.
locks.push mutates the locks state array.
The push return value (new length) minus one is assigned to local id.
Local id is used as the mapping key for the lockToOwner write.
_message is embedded in the LoveBlock appended by locks.push.
_encrypted is embedded in the LoveBlock appended by locks.push.
ownerToNumber.add(1) invokes the SafeMath library function add.
myLoveBlockCount indexes ownerToNumber with msg.sender, making the result caller-dependent.
myLoveBlockCount reads ownerToNumber[msg.sender].
totalLoveBlocks reads the length of the locks array.
myLoveBlocks uses ownerToNumber[msg.sender] to size the result array.
myLoveBlocks compares msg.sender against lockToOwner[i] to filter owned locks.
myLoveBlocks allocates the memory result array.
Loop index i reads the lockToOwner mapping.
Owned lock indices read from lockToOwner are written into result.
counter determines the write position within result.
result array is returned from myLoveBlocks.
The loop variable i controls iteration over the locks array in myLoveBlocks.
SafeMath.add computes local c = a + b before the assert check.
Parameter a flows into the SafeMath.add computation.
Parameter b flows into the SafeMath.add computation.

normalization_plan.reason: The _message parameter only feeds the LoveBlock appended by locks.push, so it can be normalized into that unsafe operation.
The _encrypted parameter only feeds the LoveBlock appended by locks.push, so it can be normalized into that unsafe operation.
Local id is a temporary value used solely as the key of the lockToOwner storage write.
The result array is an internal temporary that only carries the return value of myLoveBlocks.
The counter local is a loop bookkeeping value used only inside myLoveBlocks.
The loop index i is a temporary iteration variable used only inside myLoveBlocks.
Parameter a is an operand consumed only by the SafeMath.add function body.
Parameter b is an operand consumed only by the SafeMath.add function body.
Local c is the transient sum/return value computed inside SafeMath.add.
